BlackRock put more than $400 million of its own capital into an $82 billion BCRED private-credit fund after redemption requests hit $3.7 billion.
Cliffwater’s $33 billion flagship fund capped redemptions at 7%.
Morgan Stanley’s North Haven Private Income Fund had a similar problem and reportedly returned less than half of what investors requested.
That seems to be the theme.

The weak point especially appears to be software. Software and technology reportedly make up about 25% of the private-credit market.
Some think AI disruption exposure could be as high as 25% to 35%.
SaaS multiples were around 24 times at the end of last year and fell to around 18 times by 2025. The median now sits closer to 16 times.
That makes a lot of older software loans look less comfortable than they were when they were originally established.
The market reaction has been ugly. More than $265 billion in market capitalization has reportedly been erased across alternative-asset managers.

There’s a lot going on here, and again, there are industry-wide ramifications.
